1	# LOOM portal: interface for agents
2	
3	This page is for an agent (or the developer of one) that needs part of a
4	person's health context to do a task for them. It is the only document an
5	agent needs; it does not have to read LOOM's source.
6	
7	## What LOOM offers
8	
9	LOOM holds one person's health record and hands out **task-scoped,
10	expiring slices** of it. You say what task you are doing; LOOM decides
11	how deep you may see, which fields you get, and for how long.
12	
13	| Tier | What it contains | Field names |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| L0 | raw sensor signal | `raw_signal` |
16	| L1 | readings (here: hourly glucose, mg/dL) | `readings` |
17	| L2 | patterns and alerts derived from readings | `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` |
18	| L3 | plain-language constraints | `constraints` |
19	
20	L0 is the deepest (most revealing), L3 the shallowest. A tier includes the
21	shallower ones: an L2 grant may carry `constraints` too.
22	
23	## Access
24	
25	- Base URL and namespace are given to you by whoever runs the portal (for
26	  a test: `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and a namespace such as `demo`).
27	  Every call for one person goes to `/v1/<namespace>/...`.
28	- There is no login in v0.1. You identify yourself with `agent_id` (this
29	  agent instance) and `publisher` (the company or developer that ships
30	  it). In Nanda Town the gateway fills `agent_id` from the signed envelope;
31	  over plain HTTP both are claims.
32	- JSON in, JSON out. Errors are JSON `{"error": "..."}`; a malformed body
33	  gets HTTP 400 naming the missing fields.
34	
35	## Endpoints
36	
37	| Method and path | Use |
38	|---|---|
39	| `GET /health` | version and policy id |
40	| `POST /v1/<ns>/requests` | ask for access for a task; a grant carries data immediately |
41	| `POST /v1/<ns>/fetch` | get fresh data again under a grant you already hold |
42	| `GET /v1/<ns>/credit` | publisher → credit score (only publishers that have been seen) |
43	| `GET /v1/<ns>/log` | every decision so far, in order |
44	| `GET /v1/policy` | the built-in tasks, as JSON (same as the table below) |
45	| `GET /v1/<ns>/proposals/<proposal_id>` | status of a proposal for a task that is not built in (see below) |
46	
47	### `POST /v1/<ns>/requests`: body
48	
49	| Field | Required | Meaning |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| `request_id` | yes | unique per request; reuse it only to retry the same request |
52	| `agent_id` | yes | your agent instance |
53	| `publisher` | yes | who ships you |
54	| `category` | yes | `agent_for_user` (works for the person) or `care_provider` (clinician side) |
55	| `task` | yes | one of the task names below |
56	| `purpose` | no | free text, recorded |
57	| `tier` | yes | the deepest tier you ask for (`L0`..`L3`) |
58	| `fields` | yes | list of field names you ask for |
59	| `at` | yes | current time on the person's timeline, in days (number) |
60	
61	### Tasks (policy `loom-policy-0.2.0`)
62	
63	| `task` | `category` | Deepest tier | Fields you may ask for | Validity |
64	|---|---|-

input.command:
mkdir -p /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run2/out && cat > /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run2/out/grocer-1.md <<'EOF'
# This week's grocery list (day 0)

Prepared by grocer-1 (freshcart). Built around two health constraints from your LOOM record: **limit added sugar** and **prefer low-glycemic foods**.

> **Please confirm before anyone shops from this.** LOOM marked this grant `confirmation: first_request`, meaning you should OK the list before it's acted on. Nothing has been ordered.

## Produce
- Leafy greens: spinach, kale or mixed salad greens (2 bags)
- Broccoli (2 heads) and cauliflower (1 head)
- Bell peppers (4), zucchini (3), cucumbers (2)
- Tomatoes (1 lb) and cherry tomatoes (1 pint)
- Onions (3), garlic (1 bulb), fresh ginger
- Green beans or asparagus (1 lb)
- Avocados (3)
- Berries: blueberries, strawberries or raspberries (2 pints) – lower-GI fruit
- Apples or pears (4) – whole fruit, eaten with protein or fat
- Lemons (2)

## Protein
- Eggs (1 dozen)
- Chicken breast or thighs (2 lb)
- Salmon or other fatty fish (1 lb), or canned salmon/sardines in water (2 cans)
- Firm tofu or tempeh (1 block)
- Plain Greek yogurt, **unsweetened** (32 oz)

## Legumes, whole grains and starches (low-GI picks)
- Dried or canned lentils and chickpeas (no-salt-added cans; 2 each)
- Black beans (2 cans)
- Steel-cut or rolled oats (not instant flavored packets)
- Quinoa or pearl barley (1 bag)
- 100% whole-grain or sourdough bread – check label for no added sugar
- Sweet potatoes (3) – instead of white potatoes

## Pantry and fats
- Extra-virgin olive oil
- Unsalted nuts: almonds, walnuts (1 bag each)
- Chia or ground flax seeds
- Natural peanut or almond butter – ingredients: nuts (+ salt) only, no added sugar
- Canned diced tomatoes / passata with no added sugar
- Spices: cinnamon, cumin, paprika, black pepper, dried herbs
- Unsweetened almond or soy milk (optional)

## Drinks
- Sparkling water (unsweetened)
- Unsweetened tea or coffee

## Skip or swap this week
| Instead of | Choose |
|---|---|
| Sweetened yogurt, flavored oatmeal packets | Plain yogurt / plain oats + berries and cinnamon |
| Juice, soda, sweetened iced tea | Sparkling water, unsweetened tea |
| White bread, white rice, regular pasta | Whole-grain/sourdough bread, quinoa, barley, lentil or chickpea pasta |
| Granola, breakfast cereals with sugar | Oats, nuts and seeds |
| Bottled sauces/dressings with sugar | Olive oil + lemon/vinegar, no-sugar-added tomato sauce |
| Cookies, candy, pastries | Berries, nuts, a square of 85%+ dark chocolate |

Label tip: in the ingredients, watch for sugar under other names – cane syrup, corn syrup, dextrose, maltose, honey, agave, fruit juice concentrate.

## What I got from LOOM and how I used it
- **Request:** task `shopping_list`, category `agent_for_user`, tier **L3**, field `constraints` only, at day 0 – exactly what the task allows. I did not ask for glucose readings or patterns; a grocery list doesn't need them, and the policy doesn't allow them for this task.
- **Decision:** `granted` (grant `g-22ecac0724`), single use, expires day 0. freshcart's credit went 60 → 61. I made no further fetches.
- **Data received:** two constraints – `limit_added_sugar` and `prefer_low_glycemic`.
- **How I used it:** every item is either naturally free of added sugar or flagged to check the label; starches are low-GI choices (legumes, oats, barley, quinoa, sweet potato, whole grains), fruit leans toward berries and whole fruit, and the swap table removes common sugar sources. Quantities are generic estimates for one person for a week.
- **What I didn't get:** no allergies, dietary preferences, medications, budget or household size – LOOM didn't provide them and I didn't guess. Adjust the list if any of those apply.
- **Friction:** confirmation band `first_request` – you should confirm this list before it's used to place an order.
EOF

input.message: As grocer-1 (publisher freshcart), I read only /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/AGENT_INTERFACE.md and opened no other files. I made one LOOM request to namespace coldstart-2 at day 0: task `shopping_list`, category `agent_for_user`, tier L3, fields `["constraints"]`. That is the most this task is allowed to ask for, so there was no overreach. It was granted (grant g-22ecac0724, single use, expires day 0) and freshcart's credit went from 60 to 61. The data came back as two constraints: `limit_added_sugar` and `prefer_low_glycemic`. I made no further fetches and didn't ask for glucose readings or patterns, since a grocery list doesn't need them. The grant's friction band is medium with `confirmation: first_request`, so the list says clearly that the person should confirm it before anyone shops from it, and nothing was ordered. The list is written to /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run2/out/grocer-1.md. It's a one-person weekly list sorted by store section: low-GI starches like legumes, oats, barley, quinoa and sweet potato; berries and whole fruit; unsweetened dairy and other staples; a "skip or swap" table for common added-sugar items; and a label tip listing other names for sugar. It ends with the required "What I got from LOOM and how I used it" section, which also notes that LOOM gave nothing on allergies, preferences, budget or household size, so I didn't make assumptions about any of those.
